newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Sept 1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Sept 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Findland's Tommi Makinen has realised his dream of winning the 1996 world drivers' championship with a victory in the rugged Rally Australia. Makinen powered around the 25 stages in his Mitsubishi a minute faster than Sweden's Kenneth Eriksson. Page 16.

Rugby league has again been hurled into controversy by comments from Sydney City chief executive Berine Gurr, who suggested taking legal action against referees for poor on-field performances with the whistle. Referee chief Mick Stone has savaged Gurr's comments, claiming they will discourage recruitment. Page 16.

Australian champion motorcycle rider Mick Doohan has again snatched a world championship title, installing him as a successive three-time winner, after finishing second in Barcelona. Doohan has admitted that Spanish team-mate Alex Criville ensured it was his most difficult title to win. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Injured Bears star-winger Brett Dallas will have to prove to coaching staff that he is up to rugby league finals football for the clash with the Dragons this weekend. With the consistency of the success of the high ball throughout the finals so far, it is doubtless that Dallas' ability to fly for the ball will be paramount. Page 45.

AAMI Cup minor premiers Warringah will be in trouble for the finals with the other major clubs boasting the return of their big guns. The presence of Matt Burke's exocet-tackling and radar-goal kicking on Friday night against Easts is unmatched in the Rats camp, who have done so well this season due to the numbers of players unavailable to the other clubs. Page 45.

Tony "Plugger" Lockett, the flavour of the month in Sydney, was scrutinised by the press last night at training while he practised passing and drill kicks. He did not attempt any kicks at goal and was visibly seen to be wincing from knee pain. Page 46.
THE AGE

Melbourne football club's potential saviour, mining tycoon Joe Gutnick, told members he will increase his financial commitment to the Demons as an angry crowd at the Dallas Brooks Hall expressed outrage over the proposed merger with Hawthorn. Page C12.

Ron Barassi, ex-Melbourne football legend, has changed his mind about his support for the proposed merger of the Melbourne and Hawthorn football clubs, reneging upon his view that it will advance the game Australia-wide. Page C12.

Adelaide captain, and bronze winning Olympian, Rachael Sporn has continued her outstanding run this season by winning the Women's National Basketball League's most-valuable player for the year, outstripping nearest rival Jenny Whittle of Brisbane by six votes. Page C10.
HERALD SUN

North Melbourne veteran Mathew Armstrong is expected to win a recall for Saturday's AFL preliminary final clash with Brisbane at the Cricket Ground, because of Stuart Anderson's unlucky hamstring strain at a training session. Page 80.

Sydney jockey Darren Beadman, who has seen great success upon Horse-of-the Year Octagonal, will again take charge of the Big O this weekend at Moonee Valley for the Feehan Stakes over 1600 metres. Beadman replaces luckless jockey Darren Gauci for the champion horse's last grab at continuing a racing career. Page 78.

Classy Essendon half-forward Mark Mercuri will have extensive treatment in a hyperbaric chamber this week for a badly inflamed back in an attempt to play in Saturday's preliminary final against Sydney - he has not yet been ruled out by team doctors. Page 8.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Sacked International golf team captain David Graham said he was glad the team had not won the President's Cup, in an outburst which could only be described as sour grapes from the Aussie who boasts US Open and PGA championships. Page 60.

St George has retreated to the videos in an attempt to find a weakness in North Sydney's defence, whilst simultaneously searching for methods for shutting down the Bears' key strike players. The Saints-Bears May game resulted in a 42-Nil drubbing of the Saints. Page 60.

Filante and Nothin' Leica Dane are early favourites for the AJC's spring carnival features, the Epsom Handicap and the Metropolitan, although they are not definite starters as yet. Doubtlessly the weights and the rest of the field in the big meets are keeping trainers cautious. Page 54.
